The slip is a 2u moon round robin, all three legs 0 HR, so it graded a clean -2.00u. Backed out of both the board and the ledger: cats.moon 335/45 +489.82u on 670.0 -> 334/45 +491.82u on 668.0; the night -22.00u -> -20.00u; season history tail -> 488.67. Verified by re-running grade_night.grade_ticket() with homered/played rebuilt from calibration.jsonl, which reproduced the recorded -22.00u exactly before anything was changed. 2026-08-28 stays in graded_nights -- it was graded. This is NOT the soccer-leftover case: those slips were published and bettable and stay in the ledger; this one had already been removed during the slate and only reappeared because of a code change. | 2026-09-02: 09-01 moon 'The Apollo' RESTORED TO THE LEDGER as a correction. The slip (2u round robin by 2s & 3 -- Kyle Stowers +269 / JJ Bleday +300 / Coby Mayo +300, anchored by Stowers) was on the board from the 5:58pm build and LOCKED from 6:43pm, then DELETED at 6:58pm when Baltimore posted a card without Mayo and assembleClient's scratch filter dropped the whole locked slip. A removed slip does not grade, so the ledger recorded nothing -- not a loss, an absence. Restoring it in D_2026-09-01.json was attempted and is IMPOSSIBLE after the fact: grade_night.py runs unconditionally and FIRST in pull-slate.yml, above the `fresh` gate, so the night folded on the 1:08am build minutes after the last out; there is no window. Graded through the live grade_ticket with RRVOID in force: Stowers 4 PA / 1 HR, Bleday 4 PA / 0 HR, Mayo NO plate appearance -> his leg VOIDS and the slip reduces onto the survivors. 4 combinations at 0.5u; the two carried by Stowers alone return 3.69 each; 1.845 - 2.00 = -0.16u. Under the pre-RRVOID rule it books a flat -2.00, so RRVOID is worth +1.84u here -- its first live money. moon: graded 365->366, staked 730.0->732.0, units 543.11->542.95; history[-1] carried the same -0.16 so the tracker total and the sparkline agree. ROOT CAUSE STILL LIVE: the scratch filter deletes a LOCKED slip wholesale (`if(t.locked){_killed[t.name]=1;return false;}`). CHALKLOCK-2026-08-29 fixed this exact shape on the chalk path; the scratch path never got it. Until it does, a scratched non-anchor leg destroys the record of a placed bet and it cannot be put back.
